The hook (.claude/hooks/command-parity-check.sh:15 `exit 0 always`, :23-26 silent skip without jq) is registered only as a PostToolUse hook in .claude/settings.json:19, and ci.yml:217-223 explicitly says nothing in CI runs it beyond shellcheck. Parts (3)/(4) of the proposal (arg-struct fields vs params, return types) need param-list parsing and common.rs resolution, so effort M is honest.

title: Docs-only CI detector skips the very tests that pin AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md and the commit hook
rationale: Five tests exist precisely to catch a malformed `## [X.Y.Z]` header, an AGENTS.md over its 20 000-byte budget, a scope added to AGENTS.md but not the hook (or vice versa), and a newest-CHANGELOG-header/version mismatch. Every one of those files is classified docs-only, so a PR that changes only one of them merges green with `just test` skipped, and the failure surfaces on the next unrelated code PR (or, for the CHANGELOG header, at release time as fallback updater notes). The `.claude/*` rule also skips the test that pins `conventional-commit-validator.sh` to AGENTS.md — the scan job only shellchecks it.
proposal: Add an exceptions arm ahead of the docs globs in the `case`: `AGENTS.md|CHANGELOG.md|.claude/hooks/*) code=true ;;` (optionally `.claude/settings.json` too, since the hooks it wires are part of the contract). Update the `changes` job comment and `.claude/rules/release-and-dependencies.md:23` ("Docs-only changes (`*.md`, `docs/`, `.claude/`) skip the compile jobs") to name the exceptions. Expected effect: the pinned invariants run on exactly the PRs that can break them; docs/ and README-only PRs stay fast.
verifier_notes: Evidence real: ci.yml:74-77 classifies `*.md` and `.claude/*` as non-build; the rust job's test step is gated on `code == 'true'` (ci.yml:128-130). release.rs pins exactly those files: CHANGELOG.md at :55, :179, :323; AGENTS.md at :119, :217; conventional-commit-validator.sh at :228. Nothing else runs them: the scan job (ci.yml:222-223) only shellchecks hooks, and the staleness-check hook is local-only for Claude Code users. db600f0 is a real docs-only CHANGELOG commit (CHANGELOG.md + docs/CHANGELOG-archive.md). .claude/rules/release-and-dependencies.md:23 documents the rule the reviewer wants amended. No AGENTS.md/doc rationale claims these files are exempt; the `changes` job comment (ci.yml:34-39) simply did not consider pinned-by-test docs. Proposal (`AGENTS.md|CHANGELOG.md|.claude/hooks/*) code=true ;;` ahead of the docs arm) is minimal and correct; `.claude/rules/*.md` can stay docs-only (not pinned).

title: Rollover guard logic (five error codes) has no test coverage because it is only reachable through State-bound commands
rationale: The arch doc calls these guards out by name ("refuses a thumbprint that is missing or expired; activating the already-active certificate is a no-op; retire refuses the active certificate ... and the staged one"), and the expired-but-still-nominated message variant is a deliberate UX decision — yet none of it is asserted. `build_rollover` is thoroughly table-tested; the decisions layered on top of it are not, so a refactor could swap `cert_is_active`/`cert_is_staged`, drop the idempotent activate, or invert the expired check without a failing test.
proposal: Extract two pure functions next to `build_rollover`: `retire_target<'a>(roll: &'a SigningCertRolloverDto, key_id: &str) -> Result<&'a SigningCertDto, UiError>` and `activation_target<'a>(roll: &'a SigningCertRolloverDto, thumbprint: &str) -> Result<Option<&'a SigningCertDto>, UiError>` (None = already active, no-op). Have `retire_saml_signing_certificate` and `set_preferred_signing_key` call them. Table-test every code and both `cert_is_active` messages using the existing `sp_with`/`cred` fixtures.
verifier_notes: Evidence real. The five codes appear only at their definition sites (sso/mod.rs:936, 951, 955, 1248, 1254); a repo-wide grep including apps/desktop/web-rs/tests and web-rs/src finds no test or GUI-test reference. The expired-but-nominated message variant (mod.rs:941-950) and the idempotent activate (mod.rs:1258-1260) are documented behaviours in docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md yet unasserted, while `build_rollover` is table-tested extensively (mod.rs:1949-2130). Both guards are pure decisions over a `SigningCertRolloverDto` plus a key/thumbprint, so the proposed `retire_target`/`activation_target` extraction is straightforward and reuses the existing `sp_with`/`cred` fixtures. Medium kept: these guards are what stop an operator from deleting the certificate that signs assertions today.

title: Trust/redirect validation rules check the validator at module granularity, not per command — the helper-bleed the suite was rewritten to remove
rationale: `src` here is the whole module. `sso/mod.rs` already contains `validate_redirect_uri`, so a 19th command there that builds `ApplicationWebPatch {` straight from its input passes this rule; likewise a new command in `applications/federated.rs` constructing `FederatedCredentialRequest {` passes because the module imports the validator for its siblings. Feasibility caveat: writes and validators often sit in module-local helpers (`check_federated_credential` federated.rs:57, `checked_uris` restore.rs:65, sso/mod.rs:307/695/1712), so the per-command rewrite must resolve one helper level as the proposal says — effort is M rather than S. title: FilterChip (14 sites) conveys its active facet by class only — no aria-pressed/selected state
rationale: The facet chips are the primary filter control on all three list views (docs: 'Per-list filter state ... facet chips'); a keyboard/AT user cannot tell which facet is applied because the only signal is a CSS class. The sort toggles beside them already do it right with aria-pressed, so the inconsistency is within one toolbar.
proposal: Add `aria-pressed=move || facet.with(|f| f == value).to_string()` to the chip button (the chip strip is a single-select facet, so `role="radiogroup"` + `aria-checked` on the container is the stricter alternative). One line in the primitive; all 14 sites inherit. Add a GUI assertion alongside the existing facet tests.
verifier_notes: filter_chip.rs:39-56 conveys the active facet only via the `filter-chip--active` class; the `<button>` has `class`, `type`, `prop:disabled`, `on:click` and nothing ARIA. The sort toggles in the same toolbar do it right at application_list.rs:526-529 (`aria-pressed=move || active().to_string()` with a warning comment). The primitive's own doc (filter_chip.rs:1-17) explains why it is a `<button>` rather than a thaw Tab, so one `aria-pressed` line in the primitive is the correct place and every caller inherits. No GUI test references `filter-chip`, so the change is test-safe. `role="radiogroup"`+`aria-checked` is stricter but would need a container the callers own; `aria-pressed` is the minimal honest fix.

title: `rust` matrix job boots three runners on docs-only changes just to echo; other jobs skip at job level
evidence:
.github/workflows/ci.yml:86-103
  rust:
    name: Rust workspace (${{ matrix.os }})
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    ...
      - uses: actions/checkout@...
      - name: Skip notice (docs-only change)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.code != 'true'
        run: echo "Docs-only change — backend build/test skipped."

.github/workflows/ci.yml:134-137 (web job)
    # Skipped on the weekly cron (audit/deny only) and on docs-only changes. A
    # skipped job reports its required check as satisfied, so the merge gate stays
    # green without running the WASM build / GUI tests.
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule' && needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'
rationale: Two different mechanisms achieve the same required-check outcome: the rust job runs on ubuntu, windows AND macos (checkout + 7 conditional steps each, ~1 min of macOS runner per docs PR) while web/actionlint/audit/deny use a job-level `if` whose comment states that a skipped job satisfies the required check. The `changes` job header (lines 34-39) describes only the rust-job mechanism, so the file contradicts itself about how skipping works.
proposal: Move the rust job to the same job-level `if: github.event_name != 'schedule' && needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'`, drop the per-step `if:`s and the notice step, and update the `changes` job comment to describe the job-level skip. Expected effect: zero runner minutes on docs-only PRs for the matrix, one consistent pattern.
verifier_notes: ci.yml:86-130: rust job has job-level `if: github.event_name != 'schedule'` only, then a checkout, a 'Skip notice' step (:101-103) and six per-step `if: needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'` guards across a 3-OS matrix; web (:137), actionlint (:184), audit (:250) and deny (:272) use a job-level `if` whose comments (:134-136, :182-183, :249, :271) state that a skipped job satisfies the required check — the same GitHub semantics the rust job could use. The `changes` job comment (:34-39) describes only the per-step mechanism, so the file is internally inconsistent about how skipping works. No documented reason for the asymmetry. Cost is real but small (three runner boots, one macOS, per docs-only PR); severity low.

    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "apps/desktop/web-rs/**"
      - "justfile"
      - ".github/workflows/pages.yml"

apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml:25-26
  azapptoolkit-core = { path = "../../../crates/azapptoolkit-core" }
  azapptoolkit-dto = { path = "../../../crates/azapptoolkit-dto" }

apps/desktop/web-rs/build.rs:25: `let changelog = repo_root(&manifest).join("CHANGELOG.md");` (bakes the "What's new" panel)
rationale: The demo bundle compiles `azapptoolkit-core` (audit scoring, scoping, thumbprints, settings types) and `azapptoolkit-dto` into the wasm, and bakes the current version's CHANGELOG section. A merge to main that changes only those crates — e.g. a new audit finding or a DTO field the demo fixtures already carry — leaves https://tiredithumans.github.io/azapptoolkit/ showing the previous behaviour until some unrelated web-rs file changes. The CI web job does rebuild on such changes (its detector is path-agnostic), so the drift is Pages-only and silent.

Severity lowered: the demo's audit items are pre-scored fixtures delivered by the mock IPC, so most core-only changes (e.g. a scoring rule) do not alter what the demo displays; drift is real but narrow.

title: time dependency is undocumented and leaks across the cert.rs boundary into a chrono-only codebase
rationale: `time` is genuinely required: rcgen 0.14's `CertificateParams.not_before/not_after` are `time::OffsetDateTime`. But the manifest gives no hint, so the next reviewer asks the same "two time crates?" question, and `GeneratedCert` exposes `time::OffsetDateTime` publicly, pushing the second date library (and a manual unix-timestamp round-trip) into a command layer that otherwise uses chrono exclusively.
proposal: Add a one-line comment at Cargo.toml:88 ("rcgen's validity fields are time::OffsetDateTime; chrono everywhere else"), and convert inside cert.rs so `GeneratedCert.not_after` is `chrono::DateTime<Utc>` — making `time` a private detail of the one module that needs it and removing the conversion at credentials.rs:140-141.
verifier_notes: Verified: apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:88 `time = "0.3"` sits under the heavily-commented crypto block (rcgen, aws-lc-rs, p12-keystore each carry rationale) with no comment; cert.rs:22 `use time::{Duration, OffsetDateTime}`, :54 `pub not_after: OffsetDateTime`, :119-121 sets rcgen's `not_before`/`not_after`; credentials.rs:140-141 round-trips through `unix_timestamp()` into chrono. The only other consumer of `GeneratedCert.not_after` is the unit test at cert.rs:261 (`> OffsetDateTime::now_utc()`), which would move to chrono trivially. chrono is already a src-tauri dep (Cargo.toml:39). `time 0.3.55` stays in the graph via rcgen/x509-parser/cookie regardless, so this is about manifest clarity and keeping the second date library private to cert.rs. No architecture doc mentions the `time` crate (grep of docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md). Proposal feasible and low-risk.

rationale: The unit of the cap changed from one site to one chunk of 100 sites (so up to 600 site reads can be in flight across 30 $batch requests, not 6), and progress granularity is per chunk. rationale: This is the first thing a contributor (or an agent) reads about the transport. title: DEVELOPMENT.md says `just setup` warns about a missing C toolchain; neither setup script checks for one
evidence:
docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:27-30
  System dependencies that no `cargo`/`rustup` command can install — `just setup` detects and warns about
  these, but you provide them via your OS package manager:
  - A C toolchain: MSVC on Windows, Xcode CLT on macOS, gcc/clang on Linux

scripts/setup.ps1:39-45 (the only system-dep check on Windows)
  Write-Info "Checking WiX Toolset (required only for MSI packaging)"
  if (Get-Command candle -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { ... }

`grep -n -i 'link.exe\|cl.exe\|xcode\|gcc\|clang\|cc ' scripts/setup.sh scripts/setup.ps1` → none
rationale: The most common first-build failure on Windows is `linker 'link.exe' not found` (MSVC Build Tools missing) and on macOS `xcrun: error: invalid active developer path`. The doc promises `just setup` detects these; it does not — it only checks apt packages on Debian-family Linux and WiX on Windows — so the contributor hits an opaque linker error from `cargo check` (after this fix lands, from `just check`) with no pointer to the remedy.
proposal: Add a cheap probe to each script before the smoke build: Windows `Get-Command link.exe` / `cl.exe` (or `where.exe link`) → warn with the Visual Studio Build Tools link; setup.sh `command -v cc || command -v clang || command -v gcc` and on Darwin `xcode-select -p` → warn with `xcode-select --install`. Keep them warnings (non-fatal) like the existing package checks. Alternatively soften DEVELOPMENT.md to say only Linux apt packages and WiX are detected.
verifier_notes: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:27-30 promises `just setup` 'detects and warns about' a C toolchain (MSVC / Xcode CLT / gcc-clang). scripts/setup.sh checks only Debian apt packages (:29-46) and scripts/setup.ps1 only WiX (:39-45); `grep -i 'link.exe\|cl.exe\|xcode\|gcc\|clang\|cc ' scripts/*` finds nothing. So the doc overstates what setup does. Severity lowered from medium: rustup's own Windows installer prompts for the MSVC Build Tools, and the linker error is a common, searchable failure; the fix is either a cheap non-fatal probe (as proposed) or a one-line doc correction. Both are small; the doc correction alone is sufficient to make the claim honest.
